rationale: The continuous financing-deficit z-score is a defensible (not merely cosmetic) fix to the archived binary version's zero-mass problem and the signs are internally consistent, but because RANK is non-negative the signal's variation is dominated by the deficit term alone — itself close to the published external-financing/net-financing anomaly — so any result will need a horse race against the standalone deficit measure.

target_name: Expansion beyond replacement at low cash profitability
rationale: Capex-to-depreciation is a genuinely different investment-intensity benchmark than growth rates and the sign logic is coherent, but the construct is close to the well-documented investment-conditional-on-profitability (q-theory) interaction, and the non-negative RANK gate means the signed cash-ROA leg will drive most of the dispersion.

The multiplicative form is internally inconsistent with the stated reasoning — headcount cuts by productivity-improving firms produce a positive (bearish) signal identical to hiring by productivity-declining firms, the exact opposite of what the proposal claims — and the emp plus five-year sale/emp trend requirement will likely thin coverage further.

Signs are internally consistent and retained-earnings-to-assets is a distinct maturity/cumulative-profit dimension not in the archive, but the signal risks being a repackaging of two strong published anomalies (share issuance and RE-based profitability) whose product may add nothing beyond issuance alone.

target_name: Peak investment validated by earnings quality
rationale: Because TS_RANK is bounded in [0,1] while the quality z-score carries the sign and most of the dispersion, this is largely an attenuated version of the well-known profitability-plus-earnings-stability composite, so a positive result would be confounded with the quality anomaly rather than evidence of a conditional productive-investment premium.

A dense, self-scaling wedge that plausibly extends the archive's only winner and avoids the rank-attenuation trap, though it edges toward the published asset-growth anomaly with a profit-growth control, and growth in gross profit is unstable for firms with near-zero or negative gross profit even after 1% winsorization.
